description.narrative: Blue Mediterranean Partnership (BMP) is an initiative led by EBRD enabling investment along the southern and eastern Mediterranean coast and around the Red Sea that develop the blue economy, protect biodiversity and contribute to emission reductions and climate change adaptation. Participating banks (AFD, EBRD, EIB, KfW, CdP) will be able to propose support for investments in the areas of e.g. water treatment, waste management, coastal tourism, marine renewable energy, sustainable ports and shipping, and climate adaptation of vulnerable coastal areas.

Blue Mediterranean Partnership (BMP) är ett initativ lett av EBRD som avser att möjligöra investering längs den södra och östra medelhavskusten som utvecklar den blåekonomin, skyddar biologisk mångfald och bidrar till klimatagendan. Deltagande banker (AFD, EBRD, EIB, KfW CdP) kan föreslå projekt för stöd inom t.ex. vattenrening, avfallshantering, kustnära hållbar turism, förnybar marinenergi, hållbara hamnar och klimatanpassning av kustområden.

The BMP fund has started to ramp up its investment support with a total of five projects approved during 2025 and the first two months of 2026. Approved projects range several different thematic areas and with a geographic coverage spanning all three of the current beneficiary countries. The projects are listed below for a total of :
Partner | Project | Amount (Euro)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- AFD | East Alexandria Wastewater Treatment and Sludge Management | 2 060 000
EIB | Offshore Wind project in Morocco (EIB) | 2 060 000
ERBD | Ayla Oasis Regeneration Project Aqaba | 508 000
EBRD | Rosetta Wall Rehabilitation Project | 824 000
AFD | Port sanitation investments for green and resilient ports in Morocco | 2 060 000
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The approved portfolio covers a range of thematic areas identified as priorities under the BMP strategic partnership: renewable energy (wind), wastewater treatment, coastal resilience, tourism, marine transport, and the protection of the marine environment (ecosystem restoration). As previously mentioned, the projects are geographically balanced. Only one of the five projects is private-sector led, but the focus on public investments was expected. However, Sida will encourage the submission of more private-sector-focused investments for support through the trust fund.
At this stage, all projects focus on technical assistance for upstream design and feasibility work. As the partnership evolves and projects become more mature, it is expected that more requests will relate to credit enhancement through investment grants or other types of financial instruments, if and when such instruments become available under the partnership.
The main priority has been the expansion of the project portfolio, which has progressed successfully. Another priority has been to expand the geographical coverage of the partnership by including new beneficiary countries. Progress in this regard has been slower, and no new countries joined during 2025. Discussions with Tunisia have not advanced; however, EBRD, acting as the secretariat, will re-engage with government counterparts during 2026 with the aim of resolving the political issues that have prevented the country from joining. Lebanon is likely to join the partnership in the near future and is expected to attend the Steering Committee meeting in April as an observer.
Sweden, together with the Union for the Mediterranean (UfM), has served as co-chair of the Steering Committee. Pipeline and portfolio development have progressed according to plan, but beneficiary countries have been less active than donors and implementing partners during meetings. Engagement and ownership may hopefully be strengthened if Jordan assumes the co-chairmanship following UfM.
The European Commission has pledged support to BMP through the Neighbourhood Investment Platform (NIP) but will not channel its contribution through the EBRD-managed trust fund. Instead, its technical assistance support will be provided through bilateral agreements with the implementing partners (partner IFIs). How this support will be coordinated with the other BMP donors remains unclear and will be followed up during the next Steering Committee meeting.
Now that a project portfolio has been successfully established, donors can be more selective and should encourage greater innovation and a higher level of ambition regarding the environmental sustainability of new projects.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
